## TL;DR

I ran a QA pass over Settings → Notifications (ntfy, the Telegram bot section, and per-chat task notifications) and fixed the problems it found. The main ones: two native `confirm()` dialogs became the shared `ConfirmDialog`; a failed chat-list load no longer looks like an empty list; the ntfy test now explains a failure; and the status line and error messages use plain English with a next step. A headless WebKit test runs the tab at 375, 768 and 1280 px against fixtures, and the QA findings are in `docs/qa/2026-11-notifications-qa.md`. Nothing contacts Telegram, no real token is used, and no token appears in the rendered page. Human checks remain: a real bot, and an ntfy test delivered to a phone.

## Work and rationale

I started from the three components the task named: `TelegramSettingsPanel.vue`, `TelegramChatNotificationsSettings.vue`, and the ntfy block in `SettingsView.vue`. I read each template and its script, then checked the server routes they call, so that each message I rewrote matched what the server actually returns.

The first decision was dialogs. AGENTS.md bans native `confirm()` in app actions, and the Telegram panel used it for disconnect and unbind. `AuthSettingsPanel` already runs the same flow through `ConfirmDialog`, so I reused that component rather than writing a new one. The unbind title names the account and email, so the user sees what will be removed. The component test that stubbed `window.confirm` had to change: it now checks that cancel sends no request, and that confirm sends the delete.

The second decision was error states. The bound-chat list swallowed its load error and fell through to the empty-state copy, so a network failure looked like "no chats." I added a separate load error, and a failed toggle now names the chat and says to try again. While tracing the toggle, I found the PATCH spread `JSON_OPTS`, which is a function, not an object. The request went out without `Content-Type: application/json`. The server reads the body regardless, so the toggle worked by accident. I changed it to `JSON_OPTS("PATCH", …)` and added a unit test that checks the header and body.

The third decision was copy. The empty state told the user to bind chats "from the admin API." That is not a next step, since there is no bind-code button in the UI. The copy now tells the user to send `/bind` plus a bind code from an administrator, and says that the code is created through the API for now. The status line showed raw enum values ("transport polling"); it now reads "checking Telegram for messages" and similar. The disabled-integration error from the server pointed at `repoos.toml`, which is useless from this screen, so I reworded it to point at the Notifications switch. Three route-test assertions match the new wording.

For ntfy, the button label alone ("✗ Failed") gave no reason and reverted after two seconds. I added a result line under the topic row that stays until the next attempt, and a hint explaining why the button is disabled. I kept the success wording honest: the server publishes without waiting for delivery, so the line says "Test sent" and tells the user what to check if nothing arrives.

Tests: the component tests cover the PATCH shape, the three error states, the empty copy, the dialogs, and the receive-mode label. The browser file, `notifications-settings-qa-browser.test.ts`, runs four cases at each of the three widths. It stubs the Telegram and ntfy endpoints, turns the switches on in a fetched `/api/config`, and aborts any request to `api.telegram.org`. It checks for horizontal overflow, page exceptions, and native dialogs. Its token check types a placeholder token, confirms it is not in `innerText` or `innerHTML`, and fails the run if it appears.

## Approaches tried

I first tried to spy on native dialogs before navigating. The `goto` reset the page window, so the spy count came back undefined. Moving the spy after navigation fixed it.

My first browser run timed out waiting for the Telegram section. The cause was not the component: `build:ui` runs `vue-tsc --noEmit && vite build`, and a type error in a test file stopped the chain before Vite emitted `dist/ui`. The server then answered `/settings` with a JSON 404. Fixing the type error fixed the browser run.

I considered adding a shared "bind code" control to close the empty-state gap. That is a new feature, not a QA fix, so I left it out and recorded it as a follow-up in the QA doc.

I considered rewording the raw "Last error:" text from `status.lastError`. Those messages come from the Telegram adapter, which already redacts tokens, so a per-error mapping would be a larger change. I left it and noted it.

## Challenges and blockers

`REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` finished with "All checks passed" (format, lint, build, rendered contrast, branch artifacts, UI smoke). The unit suite in the gate is partly remote, so the local Vitest runs above are the direct evidence for the tests. I did not look at the 375 px screenshot by eye; the overflow measurement is the only layout evidence I have, and the QA doc says so.

No human-only step blocks the code. The acceptance criteria are satisfied with fixtures, but two checks need a human: a real Telegram bot (the task forbids using real tokens here) and an ntfy test delivered to a device. Those belong in a held human task, not in this one.

## Key learnings

A component can look correct in isolation and still be wrong on the wire. The `JSON_OPTS` spread would have passed every test that mocks `api`; only checking the outgoing init caught it. Assert on the request shape, not just on the UI.

A swallowed error is worse than a visible one, because the empty state looks like a real answer. Any load path that catches and falls back to an empty list should say so.

Fixture tests need a fixture build. A browser run against an unbuilt `dist/ui` fails with a misleading 404 on a route that exists, so a failing browser run should first confirm that the build actually ran.
